info.name: Buildiq Versioning — REQ-OBV-001..005
info.description: Newman integration suite for the buildiq-versioning OpenSpec change. Exercises the snapshot-on-publish listener, the version-list filter, the diff endpoint, and the rollback (re-publish on prior manifest) flow. The collection is self-contained: it locates the seeded hello-world Application by slug, captures its UUID + current ApplicationVersion UUID into collection variables, then drives the lifecycle through publish → diff → rollback → republish. Teardown PUTs the original manifest back so the suite is idempotent.

item.name: Setup — locate the seeded hello-world Application + initial v1.0.0 snapshot
item.description: Captures the Application's uuid + its current v1.0.0 ApplicationVersion uuid so the rest of the suite can chain. Also stashes the original manifest into a collection variable for the teardown.

exec: pm.test('Nextcloud reachable', function () {
pm.response.to.have.status(200);
pm.test('OR returns the seeded Application', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });
const body = pm.response.json();
const rows = (body && body.results) || (Array.isArray(body) ? body : []);
const want = pm.collectionVariables.get('test_slug');
const app = rows.find(r => (r.slug === want || (r['@self'] && r['@self'].slug === want)));
// Fetched UNFILTERED and matched here, because OpenRegister's
// property-filter dialect differs between builds and this suite must
// not depend on which one is installed. Log the shape on a miss: an
// empty application_uuid leaves every later URL in this collection
// interpolating an empty path segment.

if (!app) { console.log('[diag] want=' + want + ' rows=' + rows.length); rows.slice(0, 8).forEach(function (r, i) { console.log('[diag' + i + '] slug=' + r.slug + ' self=' + ((r['@self'] || {}).slug) + ' k=' + Object.keys(r).slice(0, 8).join(',')); }); }
pm.test('hello-world present', function () { pm.expect(app, 'expected to find hello-world').to.not.be.undefined; });
if (app) {
const uuid = app.uuid || (app['@self'] && app['@self'].id) || app.id;
pm.collectionVariables.set('application_uuid', String(uuid));
pm.collectionVariables.set('application_id', String(app.id || (app['@self'] && app['@self'].id) || uuid));
pm.collectionVariables.set('original_manifest', JSON.stringify(app.manifest || {}));
// STASH THE WHOLE RECORD, not just the manifest.
// OpenRegister's saveObject() is PUT-SEMANTIC, not PATCH:
// fillMissingSchemaPropertiesWithNull() sets every schema property
// absent from the body to null. The Application schema declares
// `required: ['slug', 'name']`, so the partial bodies this collection
// used to PUT ({version, status, manifest} and nothing else) asked OR
// to null out both required fields — and OR refused the whole write
// with 400 Bad request. Three assertions failed on that, and none of
// them was about versioning at all.
// `@self` is dropped: it is server-owned metadata, not writable state.
const full = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(app));
delete full['@self'];
pm.collectionVariables.set('application_full', JSON.stringify(full));

item.name: 0.3 GET ApplicationVersion list — expect at least the seeded v1.0.0

exec: pm.test('Versions list returns 200', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });
const body = pm.response.json();
const rows = (body && body.results) || (Array.isArray(body) ? body : []);
pm.test('Seeded v1.0.0 ApplicationVersion exists', function () {
// The Application object exposes more than one identifier (`id`,
// `uuid`, `@self.id`) and the seed links the version by the OR uuid.
// Accept any of the captured ones rather than betting on which field
// the REST layer surfaces — a wrong guess here reads as 'the seed did
// not run', which is the misdiagnosis this suite already made once.
// ⚠️ FETCHED UNFILTERED — `?application={{uuid}}` RETURNS ZERO ROWS.
// OpenRegister does not match a RELATION property as a plain
// query-string data filter. Measured against a live instance:
//   applicationVersion?_limit=5000        -> 119 rows
//   applicationVersion?semver=1.0.0       ->  20 rows  (scalar prop: works)
//   applicationVersion?application=<uuid> ->   0 rows  (relation: does NOT)
// and the third query used a uuid taken straight out of row 1 of the
// first, so the value was demonstrably present. `application` is an
// x-openregister-relation; the filter is simply not applied to it.
// An empty result from a filter that CANNOT match looks exactly like a
// true zero — here, exactly like 'the seed never ran'. Step 0.2 already
// fetches unfiltered and matches in-script for this reason; 0.3, 1.2 and
// 3.2 did not, and five assertions in this collection failed as a result.
const ids = [pm.collectionVariables.get('application_uuid'), pm.collectionVariables.get('application_id')].filter(Boolean);
// Record how many rows this Application owns BEFORE the publish.
// REQ-OBV-002 is asserted as 'this number does not change', which is
// only meaningful if the number is also known to be non-zero — see 1.2.
pm.collectionVariables.set('versions_before_publish', String(rows.filter(r => ids.indexOf(String(r.application)) !== -1).length));
const v1 = rows.find(r => r.semver === '1.0.0' && ids.indexOf(String(r.application)) !== -1);

if (!v1) { console.log('[diagv] ids=' + JSON.stringify(ids) + ' rows=' + rows.length); rows.slice(0, 5).forEach(function (r, i) { console.log('[diagv' + i + '] semver=' + r.semver + ' app=' + r.application + ' slug=' + r.slug); }); }
pm.expect(v1, 'expected the seeded v1.0.0 row from the SeedHelloWorld repair step').to.not.be.undefined;
if (v1) {
const uuid = v1.uuid || (v1['@self'] && v1['@self'].id) || v1.id;
pm.collectionVariables.set('v1_uuid', String(uuid));

item.name: REQ-OBV-001 — publish a manifest edit triggers snapshot listener
item.description: Bump the Application's version field via OR PUT. The lifecycle's draft → published transition fires ObjectTransitionedEvent → ApplicationVersionSnapshotListener creates a new ApplicationVersion row. We assert the row appears in the list and that the Application's currentVersion is now updated.

exec: // MERGE INTO THE WHOLE RECORD — OR's PUT IS NOT A PATCH.
// This request used to send only {version, status, manifest}.
// OpenRegister's saveObject() nulls every schema property the body
// omits, the Application schema declares `required: ['slug', 'name']`,
// and the write was therefore refused with 400 Bad request. Nothing in
// that failure mentions slug or name, so it read as a versioning bug;
// three assertions in this collection failed on it.
// The same trap is spelled out in lib/Command/SeedHelloWorldFixture.php
// ('⚠️ `permissions` IS REPEATED HERE ON PURPOSE — DO NOT TRIM IT') and
// in tests/e2e/support/appRoles.ts. This is the third place it has cost
// something.
const base = JSON.parse(pm.collectionVariables.get('application_full') || '{}');
const manifest = {
version: '1.1.0',
dependencies: ['openregister'],
menu: [{ id: 'Messages', label: 'buildiq.helloworld.menu.messages', icon: 'icon-comment', route: 'Messages', order: 1 }],
pages: [
{ id: 'Messages', route: '/', type: 'index', title: 'buildiq.helloworld.title.messages', config: { register: 'buildiq', schema: 'hello-message', columns: ['title', 'body', '@self.created'] } },
{ id: 'About', route: '/about', type: 'detail', title: 'buildiq.helloworld.title.about', config: { register: 'buildiq', schema: 'hello-message' } }
pm.collectionVariables.set('merged_body', JSON.stringify(Object.assign({}, base, { version: '1.1.0', status: 'published', manifest: manifest })));
pm.test('Publish PUT accepted', function () {
pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.code === 400
? 'got 400 — OR PUT is PUT-semantic, so a partial body nulls the required slug/name; send the merged full record'
: 'the publish write must be accepted').to.be.oneOf([200, 201, 204]);
// Assert the MERGE actually held, not merely that the write returned 200.
// Without this, trimming the merge back to a partial body would fail
// somewhere else entirely and this request would still look fine.
pm.test('slug and name survived the write (PUT semantics did not null them)', function () {
const base = JSON.parse(pm.collectionVariables.get('application_full') || '{}');
const body = pm.response.json();
pm.expect(body.slug, 'slug must still be the seeded one after the publish').to.eql(base.slug);
pm.expect(body.name, 'name must still be the seeded one after the publish').to.eql(base.name);

item.name: 1.2 GET ApplicationVersion list — v1.1.0 must now appear

exec: pm.test('Versions list returns 200', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });
const body = pm.response.json();
const rows = (body && body.results) || (Array.isArray(body) ? body : []);
// ⚠️ THIS ASSERTION USED TO DEMAND THE OPPOSITE OF THE SPECIFICATION.
// It required 'the listener must have appended a v1.1.0 row'. The
// canonical spec — openspec/specs/openbuild-version-snapshots/spec.md,
// status: done — says the reverse, in these words:
//   REQ-OBV-002: 'The system SHALL NOT spawn sibling ApplicationVersion
//   rows on draft → published transitions. Snapshot-on-publish writeback
//   is retired under ADR-002.'
//   'The system SHALL NOT subscribe any PHP listener
//   (ApplicationVersionSnapshotListener or any successor)...'
//   Scenario: 'Publishing does NOT create a sibling ApplicationVersion'.
// And there is no such listener: lib/Listener/ holds six listeners and
// none is it; the only references left are an archived change proposal,
// two PHPUnit files and this collection. This collection was written
// against `buildiq-versioning` (archived 2026-05-12) and never updated
// when `buildiq-version-snapshots` superseded it.
// So the ONLY way the old assertion could have gone green was for the
// product to regress to an architecture the spec explicitly forbids.
// It now asserts REQ-OBV-002 as written.
pm.test('REQ-OBV-002: publishing does NOT spawn a sibling ApplicationVersion row', function () {
const before = Number(pm.collectionVariables.get('versions_before_publish'));
const own = rows.filter(r => r.application === pm.collectionVariables.get('application_uuid'));
// Non-vacuous on BOTH sides: a broken list read would leave `own`
// empty, and 'unchanged' would then be trivially true against a
// `before` that was also zero. Require a real row first.
pm.expect(before, 'the setup step must have seen at least one ApplicationVersion — otherwise "unchanged" proves nothing').to.be.at.least(1);
pm.expect(own.length, 'the publish must not have appended a sibling row (REQ-OBV-002)').to.eql(before);
pm.expect(own.find(r => r.semver === '1.1.0'), 'a v1.1.0 SIBLING row is exactly what ADR-002 retired').to.be.undefined;
pm.test('Append-only — v1.0.0 row still present (history not rewritten)', function () {
const v1 = rows.find(r => r.semver === '1.0.0' && r.application === pm.collectionVariables.get('application_uuid'));
pm.expect(v1, 'v1.0.0 must NOT have been deleted by the publish').to.not.be.undefined;

item.name: REQ-OBR-009 — rollback action appends a new snapshot row
item.description: Rollback is implemented as a re-publish whose payload is the old manifest blob. We PUT the v1.0.0 manifest back onto the Application (with a draft→published transition) and assert that a THIRD ApplicationVersion row appears — history is append-only per design.md Decision 3.

item.name: 3.1 POST rollback action (PUT old manifest, re-publish)

exec: // Same merge as 1.1 — OR's PUT nulls whatever the body omits, and
// `slug`/`name` are required. See 1.1's pre-request script.
const base = JSON.parse(pm.collectionVariables.get('application_full') || '{}');
const manifest = {
version: '1.0.0',
dependencies: ['openregister'],
menu: [{ id: 'Messages', label: 'buildiq.helloworld.menu.messages', icon: 'icon-comment', route: 'Messages', order: 1 }],
pages: [
{ id: 'Messages', route: '/', type: 'index', title: 'buildiq.helloworld.title.messages', config: { register: 'buildiq', schema: 'hello-message', columns: ['title', 'body', '@self.created'] } }
pm.collectionVariables.set('merged_body', JSON.stringify(Object.assign({}, base, { version: '1.0.0-rb1', status: 'published', manifest: manifest })));
pm.test('Rollback (re-publish) accepted', function () {
pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.code === 400
? 'got 400 — OR PUT is PUT-semantic, so a partial body nulls the required slug/name; send the merged full record'
: 'the rollback write must be accepted').to.be.oneOf([200, 201, 204]);
pm.test('Versions list returns 200', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });
const body = pm.response.json();
const rows = (body && body.results) || (Array.isArray(body) ? body : []);
const own = rows.filter(r => r.application === pm.collectionVariables.get('application_uuid'));
// ⚠️ BOTH OF THESE ALSO ASSERTED THE RETIRED APPEND-ONLY MODEL.
// 'At least three rows (1.0.0 + 1.1.0 + rollback)' and 'a rollback row
// like 1.0.0-rb1' both require the sibling-snapshot behaviour that
// REQ-OBV-002 says the system SHALL NOT have, and that REQ-OBV-003
// replaces: 'restoring a previous state of an ApplicationVersion MUST
// NOT be implemented by copying from a sibling snapshot row (the
// append-only snapshot model is retired under ADR-002)'. History lives
// in OR's object-time-travel ON the row, not in extra rows beside it.
// The row COUNT is therefore the invariant, not a growing tally.
pm.test('REQ-OBV-003: rollback does not append rows — history lives in OR time-travel', function () {
const before = Number(pm.collectionVariables.get('versions_before_publish'));
pm.expect(before, 'the setup step must have seen at least one ApplicationVersion — otherwise "unchanged" proves nothing').to.be.at.least(1);
pm.expect(own.length, 'neither the publish nor the rollback may spawn sibling ApplicationVersion rows').to.eql(before);
pm.test('no append-only rollback row (e.g. 1.0.0-rb1) was created', function () {
const rollback = own.find(r => (r.semver || '').startsWith('1.0.0') && r.semver !== '1.0.0');
pm.expect(rollback, 'a 1.0.0-rb1 style sibling row is exactly what ADR-002 retired').to.be.undefined;

item.name: Teardown — restore original manifest + state
item.description: Restore the Application's manifest to the seeded value so the suite is idempotent across reruns. We intentionally do NOT delete the appended ApplicationVersion rows — the rollback test asserts append-only history, and re-running the suite simply appends more rows. This is the same convention the rbac suite uses for its seed Application (it only resets the permissions block).

exec: // Restore the ORIGINAL manifest captured in 0.2, merged into the full
// record for the same PUT-semantics reason as 1.1 and 3.1.
const base = JSON.parse(pm.collectionVariables.get('application_full') || '{}');
const original = JSON.parse(pm.collectionVariables.get('original_manifest') || '{}');
pm.collectionVariables.set('merged_body', JSON.stringify(Object.assign({}, base, { version: '1.0.0', status: 'published', manifest: original })));
pm.test('Teardown PUT accepted', function () {
pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.code === 400
? 'got 400 — OR PUT is PUT-semantic, so a partial body nulls the required slug/name; send the merged full record'
: 'the teardown write must be accepted').to.be.oneOf([200, 201, 204]);
